1.title: State: What It Is and How Terraform Uses It
1.text: Welcome to Module three: State: What It Is and How Terraform Uses It. It covers the exam area two. Terraform fundamentals. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What state is. How Terraform uses state in the workflow. Handling state safely. What happens if the state is lost or wrong. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Terraform fundamentals. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: What state is
1.text: What state is. State is Terraform's record of the infrastructure it manages. It is a Jason file (by default terraform dot tfstate in the working directory) that maps each resource in the configuration to a real object in the platform.

1.title: What state is, continued
1.text: What state is. The figure shows this: Configuration describes the goal, state remembers what exists, the plan is the difference.

1.title: What state is, continued
1.text: What state is. Mapping. Links aws instance dot web to a real instance I D. Metadata. Remembers dependencies and provider information. Performance. Caches attribute values so large setups do not need to query everything. Plan. Terraform compares configuration, state and reality to compute what to change. Exam tip: State maps configuration to real infrastructure. Without it Terraform cannot tell what it already created.

1.title: How Terraform uses state in the workflow
1.text: How Terraform uses state in the workflow. terraform plan. Reads state, refreshes it from the platform and compares with the configuration. terraform apply. Changes the infrastructure and updates the state. terraform destroy. Removes the resources and empties the state. terraform show. Displays the state or a saved plan.

1.title: Handling state safely
1.text: Handling state safely. Never edit the state file by hand. A mistake can orphan or duplicate resources; use terraform state commands. State may contain secrets. Passwords and keys appear in plain text; restrict access and encrypt the storage. Do not commit state to Git. It can leak secrets and conflicts between people. Use a remote backend for teams. Shared, locked and encrypted state (Module thirteen). Back it up. Remote backends can keep versions.

1.title: Handling state safely, continued
1.text: Handling state safely. Sensitive marking. sensitive true hides values in C L I output but they remain in state. State and terraform dot tfstate dot backup. The local backend keeps a backup of the previous state. Exam tip: State can contain sensitive data in plain text. Marking a value sensitive does not remove it from the state file.

1.title: What happens if the state is lost or wrong
1.text: What happens if the state is lost or wrong. State lost. Terraform thinks nothing exists and tries to create everything again; you must import the resources. Resource deleted outside Terraform. The next plan notices and proposes to recreate it (drift, Module fourteen). Two people apply at once. Conflicting updates; state locking prevents this (Module thirteen). Exam tip: Lost state means Terraform thinks nothing exists. The fix is to restore the state or import the resources, not to run apply again.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. What is the main role of the Terraform state? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: To map configuration to real infrastructure. State maps each resource in the configuration to a real object and caches its attributes.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A teammate wants to fix a mistake by editing terraform.tfstate with a text editor. What is the best advice? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Use terraform state commands instead. State should never be edited by hand; the terraform state commands change it safely.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A database password is stored in a resource attribute marked sensitive. Where can the value still be found? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: In the state file, in plain text. Sensitive values are hidden in C L I output but remain in the state file.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What happens when the state file is lost and the configuration is unchanged? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Terraform tries to create everything again. Without state Terraform does not know the resources exist, so it plans to create them again unless they are imported.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Why do teams use a remote backend for state? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: It allows sharing, locking and secure storage. Remote backends give shared, locked and protected state for teams.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which command displays the contents of the current state in a readable form? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: terraform show. terraform show displays the state or a saved plan.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. In what format is the default state file? Answer: Jason, in terraform.tfstate. Question two. What does state map? Answer: Configuration resources to real infrastructure objects. Question three. Can state contain secrets? Answer: Yes, in plain text.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Should state be edited by hand? Answer: No, use terraform state commands. Question five. What does a lost state cause? Answer: Terraform plans to create everything again. Question six. Which command displays state? Answer: terraform show.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. State: Jason record mapping configuration to real objects; caches attributes. Safety: never edit by hand; may hold secrets; not in Git; remote backend for teams. Lost state: Terraform plans to recreate everything; import instead. Commands: plan reads and refreshes; apply updates; show displays.
